question: When a null pointer comes from a caller's own programming mistake rather than a runtime failure, how can C code check for it, and what does another answer recommend for such a null in a language with exceptions if it signals a serious bug?
answer: In C, use an assert that is compiled out of production code; in an exception-based language, let a generic NullReferenceException bubble up to the error logging so the bug gets fixed.
support: you'll see an assert to check for the programmer errors instead of an if statement ... The generic exception is best if the error condition would be a sign of a serious bug

question: Why does the GNU sed script $a\ add a missing trailing newline to a file, and what shell test using tail -c1 and read detects that the newline is missing?
answer: sed's dump_append_queue first calls output_missing_newline even though the append queue is empty; the test is tail -c1 < "$f" | read -r _, which exits nonzero when the final newline is missing.
support: the first step is output_missing_newline ... read -r _ exits with a nonzero exit status if a trailing newline is missing

question: On Windows Server 2008, what are two ways to get at the contents of an ISO without installing third-party mounting software on the server?
answer: Extract the ISO's contents with 7-zip on the server, or mount the ISO on your workstation and copy the files over to the server to install.
support: use something like 7-zip to extract the contents of the ISO ... Mount ISO image on your workstation Copy files to server.

question: Which SSMS feature copies many tables from one server to another, what must you redo afterwards, and what SSIS option keeps transaction size small when copying multiple millions of rows?
answer: The Export Data task (Tasks > Export Data wizard); you must recreate the indices yourself; the SSIS package's batch size setting keeps transactions smaller.
support: you will have to recreate the indices yourself ... You can specify a batch size. This way your transaction size will be smaller.

question: In which ksh93 release did the exec {fd}</file style of redirection become available, and what problem with hard-coded descriptors like exec 4< does it avoid?
answer: ksh93r and above; it avoids having to pick a descriptor number and hope it is not already in use, because the shell picks a free one (10 or higher).
support: With ksh93r and above, you can open more than 10 file descriptor ... Was 4 in use? Who knows?

question: In zsh, how do you get an empty list from a glob with no matches, and in a shell loop over filenames why should the variable be prefixed with ./ before passing it to find?
answer: Use the N glob qualifier (*(N)) or setopt null_glob; prefix with ./ so a filename starting with a dash, like -test, is not parsed by find as an option.
support: Turn on the null_glob option for your pattern with the N glob qualifier ... If $f contained the filename -test, find would complain about the option

question: Which escape sequence request makes a terminal type back its Primary Device Attributes string, and which status-report query makes it reply with a sequence that bash can bind to inject text?
answer: ESC [ c (echo -e '\033[c') requests the device attributes; ESC [ 5 n makes the terminal reply ESC [ 0 n, which can be bound with bash bind to the text to insert.
support: echo -e '\033[c' ... query status report escape sequence: <ESC>[5n which terminals invariably reply (so as input) as <ESC>[0n

question: To make a bootable USB copy of a running Linux system, which command copies the root filesystem without crossing mount points, and why is running dd on a mounted live filesystem risky, and what gives a consistent copy instead?
answer: cp -ax / /mnt/sda1 copies the local filesystem; dd of a mounted filesystem can yield corruption, whereas an LVM snapshot gives a consistent point-in-time copy.
support: cp -ax / /mnt/sda1 ... you can make an LVM snapshot ... consistent snapshot of the original at a point in time

question: With a 24-hour DHCP lease, how many pool addresses would a test sending a Discover with a new spoofed MAC every five minutes tie up, and which check_dhcp option sets the MAC address to use?
answer: 288 addresses would be occupied; the -m option of check_dhcp sets the MAC address to use.
support: your Nagios test alone will occupy 288 IP addresses from your pool ... -m <mac_address_touse>

question: Which command removes duplicate lines only when they are consecutive, and how does awk '!a[$0]++' decide whether to print a line?
answer: uniq removes consecutive duplicates; the awk idiom prints a line only if a[$0] was unset or zero, i.e. first occurrence, then increments it so later duplicates fail.
support: If you can guarantee that the identical lines will be consecutive, you can use uniq ... the post-increment operator adds one to a[$0]

question: Which language is suggested for hot-patching a running game server without a restart, and what tool lets you apply a Linux kernel update without rebooting?
answer: Erlang (Java has similar functionality) is suggested for hot-patching running code; KSplice allows kernel updates without a reboot.
support: Erlang is a good choice (hotpatching example) ... You must reboot after a kernel update (unless you are using KSplice)

question: In an mdadm RAID1 pairing a fast SSD with a slow HDD, which option makes the md driver avoid reading from a device, and which option lets that device lag behind writes and what does its value set?
answer: --write-mostly makes md avoid reading from the flagged device; --write-behind lets it lag, and its value (e.g. 1024) sets the size of the write buffer.
support: the 'md' driver will avoid reading from these devices if at all possible ... the parameter determines how large the write buffer is

question: On a non-GNU sed that may not accept \n in the replacement, what fallback is suggested for inserting a line after a match, and what does the POSIX specification require after the backslash of the a command?
answer: Put a backslash then an actual newline (press Enter) in the replacement, or use perl or awk; POSIX requires a newline after a's backslash before the text.
support: then pressing Enter to get the newline ... the POSIX specification for sed requires a newline after

question: Which old 2004 Windows vulnerability illustrates that a valid-looking uploaded image can carry an attack, and how can a file named fake_image.jpg lead to XSS?
answer: The GDI JPEG vulnerability; if the file is really HTML and the browser content-sniffs it, visiting its URL directly renders it as an HTML page, enabling XSS.
support: the GDI JPEG vulnerability in Windows from 2004 ... some browsers ... will display the html page in the file

question: What is the first skill listed for a beginner sysadmin to learn, and what mechanisms make TCP reliable?
answer: How to make (and restore) backups; TCP is backed by acknowledgements (acks) and retries to ensure data gets where it is going.
support: How to make (and restore) backups! ... TCP is backed by acks and retries

question: When unit testing a handler that depends on a validator, what should you substitute and verify, and why is querying an object's state before deciding what to tell it considered poor OO design?
answer: Substitute a stub or mock validator and verify the handler calls it with the right inputs; deciding outside the object breaks encapsulation and leaks internal state.
support: you'll need a stub (or mock) validator ... the object is now a leaky abstraction; some of its behavior is located outside of the object

question: Which three InnoDB settings can be tuned to engage more CPUs, and what is usually the slowest part of a database system?
answer: innodb_read_io_threads, innodb_write_io_threads and innodb_io_capacity; the disk is usually the bottleneck of a DB system.
support: innodb_read_io_threads innodb_write_io_threads innodb_io_capacity ... Usually the bottleneck (or slowest part) of a DB system is the disk

question: Which GNU screen commands switch on background colour erase for a window and for the default of all new screens, and when did tmux implement that capability?
answer: The bce command switches it on and defbce sets the default for new screens; tmux implemented background colour erase in October 2016.
support: One switches it on with the bce command. One sets the default ... with the defbce command ... He later implemented it in October 2016

question: What happens if you leave out a join condition in a comma-style join versus an ANSI join, and what should you compare to check whether the two styles perform differently?
answer: ANSI join gives a compile-time error; the old comma syntax silently returns a CROSS JOIN. Compare the EXPLAIN plans and execution times of each style.
support: if you miss out a join condition you get a compile time error ... getting the EXPLAIN plan for each and seeing if execution time is the same

question: When building a writable snapshot overlay on a read-only loop device so LVM will activate it, how do you stop LVM complaining about duplicate PVs, and how can you check how full the overlay is?
answer: Exclude the original loop device with a filter or scan setting in /etc/lvm/lvm.conf (e.g. r|/dev/loop1|); check overlay fullness with dmsetup status on the new device name.
support: edit /etc/lvm/lvm.conf to exclude the original /dev/loop1 ... You can tell how full it is with dmsetup status
